channel.title: Lexus recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Lexus GS and RC Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank on some Lexus RC and GS vehicles may fail. If the pump fails, the engine can stall while driving.

item.title: Lexus NX Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: On certain Lexus NX, RX, and TX vehicles, the rearview camera image may fail to show up on screen when the car is shifted into reverse. This means the vehicle does not meet the federal requirement for rear visibility.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus and Subaru rearview camera may freeze
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain 2022 through 2026 Toyota and Lexus vehicles and the Subaru Solterra that have the Panoramic View Monitor camera system. Models include RAV4, Highlander, Prius, Sienna Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, Mirai, bZ4X and the Lexus NX and TX Hybrid. A software error can cause the backup camera picture to freeze or go blank when the car is in reverse, so these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard.

item.title: Lexus NX Head Restraints May Detach Unexpectedly
item.description: The head restraints on the driver and front passenger seats in these vehicles may come off without the lock release button being pressed. If a head restraint is removed this way and not put back in place, it may not be there to help protect the driver or passenger during a rear-end crash.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus SUV curtain airbags may deploy wrong
item.description: Certain Toyota Grand Highlander and Lexus TX vehicles have driver and passenger side curtain air bags that may not unroll the way they are supposed to. Instead of deploying properly to protect occupants, the air bag could partially deploy outside of an open window. This means that in a crash, the air bag may not be positioned correctly to help protect the people inside the vehicle.

item.title: Lexus LS Passenger Airbag Sensor May Misread Occupant
item.description: In certain Lexus LS500 and LS500 Hybrid vehicles with the Executive Package, the front passenger seat may have been built with parts that interfere with each other, which can cause the seat's occupant sensor to incorrectly read whether someone is sitting there.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus airbag sensor may block deployment
item.description: On certain Toyota and Lexus models, a short circuit can develop in the sensor that detects who is sitting in the front passenger seat, called the occupant classification sensor. If this happens, it can prevent the front passenger airbag from deploying in a crash.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus: Steering Cable May Disable Air Bag
item.description: On certain Toyota Corolla, Corolla Cross, Highlander, Tacoma, and related Lexus vehicles, an electrical connection inside the steering column's spiral cable assembly may not be welded well enough. If this connection separates, it can deactivate the driver's air bag. A deactivated air bag will not deploy the way it's supposed to. Dealers will inspect the spiral cable assembly and replace it if necessary, free of charge.

item.title: Lexus RX350 leftover tow hook risks fuel fire
item.description: Some Lexus RX350 vehicles left the factory with a metal transport hook still attached that should have been removed before sale. If the vehicle is hit from behind, this hook can damage the fuel filler pipe. A damaged fuel pipe can leak fuel, which raises the risk of a fire. Dealers will inspect vehicles and remove the hook if it is still present, at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus fuel pumps may fail, stalling engine
item.description: Toyota is recalling a large number of Toyota and Lexus vehicles from the 2017 through 2020 model years, including Camry, Corolla, RAV4, Highlander, Tacoma, Tundra, Sienna and many Lexus models. The low-pressure fuel pump, which sits inside the fuel tank and sends gasoline to the engine, may fail. If it fails, the engine can stall while you are driving. This recall expands an earlier recall covering the same fuel pump problem.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus fuel pump may fail, stall engine
item.description: On many Toyota and Lexus models, the low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail. If the pump fails, the engine can stall while the vehicle is being driven, which affects the driver's ability to keep control of the vehicle at that moment.

item.title: Lexus LS Run-Flat Tires Can Lose Tread
item.description: These vehicles have run-flat tires with a reinforcement layer built into the sidewall. During the process of mounting the tire onto the wheel, that layer may have cracked. A cracked layer can cause the tire's outer tread to separate from the rest of the tire while driving, which can affect how the vehicle handles and stays stable on the road.

item.title: Toyota Land Cruiser and Lexus LX570 Airbag Deactivation
item.description: On some Toyota Land Cruiser and Lexus LX 570 vehicles, a wire harness connected to the front passenger seat belt's tension sensor can break over time. If this wire breaks, it can turn off the front passenger air bag, the knee air bag, and the side air bag built into the passenger seat. These air bags would then not be available to help protect the passenger.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus vehicles carry incorrect load capacity labels
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain Toyota 4Runner, Tundra, Highlander, RAV4, Sienna and Tacoma vehicles, along with the Lexus GX460. These vehicles may have an incorrect label showing how much weight the vehicle is able to carry. Because of this, they do not meet the federal safety rule covering tire selection and rims. Toyota will contact owners and send them corrected labels at no cost.
